_comment: Supplementary well-tie CHECK spec for the same divider-chain GDS as
erc-supply-spec.json (the #103 item-11 artifact). NOT the item-11 artifact
itself: #103 -- quoting the then-open known blocker klayout-tools#2169 --
directs the canonical supply spec to omit `ties[]` so `erc.missing_tie` is
documented as not-computed rather than reported as a misleading zero, and
erc-supply-spec.json keeps that ruling. This probe exists because #2169
CLOSED upstream on 2026-09-20 (PR #2186 isolates the tie connectivity graph
from the wire/via graph, and PR #2199 grades degenerate tap declarations as
skipped rather than clean), which makes a genuinely checked well-tie verdict
expressible for the first time -- and this repo is the canary that exists to
exercise exactly that. Run at the same pinned klt build as the committed
supply report so both provenance blocks name one tool identity.
What it adds over the canonical spec, in one tie entry:
- The pfet row's n-well tie: the curated `sg13cmos5l` deck derives a well
tie as `nSD & Activ & NWell` (klayout-tools#1414, tap_nplus=(7,0)). This
probe expresses the drawn CONTACT of that tap as the boolean
`tap_layer: Cont(6/0)` narrowed by `tap_requires: [nSD(7/0)]` -- inside
the row's merged NWell (31/0) that intersection is exactly the well-tap
contact strip and provably excludes every pfet source/drain contact,
whose Cont sits on pSD-covered Activ (14/0), the opposite-doping implant.
That is the #2199 falsifiability bar: the narrowing removes real geometry,
so the tie is graded CHECKED, not skipped-degenerate.
- The substrate half of the tie question is NOT expressible as a `ties[]`
entry on this stream, and this spec does not fake it: klt erc keys a tie
on physically distinct `well_layer` shapes, and this GDS draws NO
p-well/substrate shape at all (no 46/0 PWell, no 40/0 Substrate polygon)
-- the p+ substrate-tie strip of the nfet row (pSD-covered Activ outside
every NWell, per the same deck derivation) sits in the bare global
substrate, which no declared well shape can carry. Its standing-in
evidence remains what erc-supply-spec.json's comment block names: the
compose route record (`divider_chain_nfet_w2_l0p5.substrate_tap` pinned
into VSS) and the same-record LVS `match` carrying both supplies in its
net_correspondence.
Everything else (stackup, vias, nets, label layers, layer-number provenance)
is identical to erc-supply-spec.json -- see that file's comment block for
the dual-source (PDK .lyp + curated deck table) justification of each entry.
